newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Trade slows, puts still a focus.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Trade slows, puts still a focus.

text.p: Investors continued to load up on stock index put options Thursday, even as the market struggled to recover from its recent decline.
Traders said the rangebound market led to a slowdown in trading, as did hesitation ahead of the November U.S. employment report, due early Friday.
"Attention is shifting to puts," said Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co.
He said investors were likely buying puts for protection in case of a drop Friday linked to the employement report, and also just for general protection.
In the S&P 100 stock index .OEX, the December 720 put traded 16,500 contracts and the December 725 put traded 13,300 by 1420 CST (2020 GMT).
The index itself was down 2.08 points at 722.88, having bounced between 721.26 and 727.36.
The only OEX call option to trade more than 10,000 contracts was the December 725, which traded about 15,100. The December 740 call traded 9,300.
The benchmark Dow industrial average .DJI was ahead about three points at 6,426. It reached an intraday high of 6,452 and an intraday low of 6,402.
"The market's been bouncing a little bit today," said Rod Jamieson at EVEREN Securities.
He said options investors were trying to play bounces as well as dips but trading overall had slowed from earlier in the week.
"It's starting to get to where the market's freezing up a little," he said. "Basically people are waiting around.
"Bonds got a little clocked today and everybody is waiting for the (stock) market to drop but it's hanging in there," he said.
U.S. Treasury bond futures fell sharply, leading cash prices lower as well. The selloff was linked to profit-taking and nervousness ahead of the jobs report.
Stock index futures were under pressure in afternoon but some floor traders were impressed with December S&P 500's ability to hold above their 2-1/2 week low.
Fair value narrowed to 1.25 points to cash and arbitrage buy programs were seen at a premium of 2.20 points and sell programs at a 0.50 premium.
Trading in S&P 500 .SPX options was quiet, traders said, with most action focused on the December series.
On the Chicago Board Options Exchange, the December 730 put was most active among SPX options. More than 5,150 contracts changed hands.
The option, which has seen a steady rise in open interest, was up 3/8 at 4-1/8. Open interest was 27,217.
Other actives included the December 720, 725 and 740 puts and the December 760, 765 and 770 calls.
Farther out, the January 750 call and February 750 call each traded on solid volume.
